title: severed-wire audit of src/tool_output (13 files, 5,449 LOC)

findings.title: OutputDigest::render(max_salient) budget hook left unthreaded at two live callers
findings.rationale: render(max_salient) documents max_salient as the token-budget hook ('the caller can shrink this to honour a token budget'), and MAX_SALIENT_LINES is pub(crate) precisely so callers can scale it. hygiene.rs::salient_cap (hygiene.rs:156) and result_processing.rs::inline_error_digest (result_processing.rs:501) both now scale it via scale_to_budget — but two further LIVE production consumers still pass digest.salient.len() (i.e. no cap): distill_or_truncate (result_processing.rs:471) and clean_error_body (dispatch.rs:1654). In both, the full digest is rendered first and only afterwards measured against a token/char guard; when it overshoots, the signal-aware digest is DISCARDED and the caller falls back to head+tail truncation, which drops exactly the middle-of-stream errors the distiller exists to surface. The budget_tokens value is already in scope at distill_or_truncate (its sole parameter), so the wire is missing, not the data: a live reader that reaches for a hardcoded 'no cap' instead of the budget is the config-reader-parity severed-wire shape, and the fix is the one missing call (pass a scale_to_budget-derived cap as max_salient), not new coupling. No dead scaffolding was found anywhere in this module — all 40+ pub/pub(crate) producers have live consumers, the MCP __-separator matches, and there are no // TODO / unimplemented! / todo! stubs.
